question: Transition elements are generally found in which block of the periodic table?
solution:
The correct answer is __**d-block**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Transition elements are found in the **d-block** of the periodic table, which includes elements from groups 3 to 12.
 
• These elements are characterized by the progressive filling of the d-orbitals of their atoms.
 
• The d-block elements are also referred to as transition metals and include elements such as iron (Fe), copper (Cu), and chromium (Cr).
 
• They exhibit unique properties such as variable oxidation states, the formation of colored compounds, and the ability to form complexes.
 
• The d-block elements play a crucial role in industries due to their catalytic properties and their application in alloys, electronics, and other fields.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **s-block:**

 
 
• The s-block elements are found in groups 1 and 2 of the periodic table, including alkali metals (e.g., sodium, potassium) and alkaline earth metals (e.g., magnesium, calcium).
 
• Their outermost electrons occupy the s-orbital, and they typically exhibit a single oxidation state.
 
• These elements are highly reactive, especially with water and oxygen, and are good conductors of heat and electricity.
 
 
 
• **p-block:**
 
 
• The p-block elements are located in groups 13 to 18 of the periodic table.
 
• These include non-metals (e.g., oxygen, nitrogen), metalloids (e.g., boron, silicon), and some metals (e.g., aluminum, lead).
 
• Their outermost electrons occupy the p-orbitals, and they show a wide range of chemical and physical properties.
 
• They are involved in important industrial and biological processes, such as photosynthesis and the production of fertilizers.
 
 
 
• **f-block:**
 
 
• The f-block elements are the lanthanides and actinides, found below the main body of the periodic table.
 
• They are characterized by the filling of the 4f and 5f orbitals, respectively.
 
• These elements include rare earth metals and radioactive elements like uranium and thorium.
 
• f-block elements are used in advanced technologies, such as nuclear energy production and the development of superconductors.
